Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.console

Class HtmlCardType

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.console.HtmlCardType
All Implemented Interfaces:
CardTypeHandler
public final class HtmlCardType extends Object implements CardTypeHandler
The built-in html card type: markup-only (JSON5 bodies are E-25), with an optional body auto-captured as a <template data-card="{id}">. A bare html card (no body) emits an empty fragment — the shell paints an empty .jc-card and nothing more.
Trust boundary for src:

An html card in a page contract may instead name a src endpoint. The src must be a same-origin path (checked at page build, by PageCapture.addCard for FreeMarker and PageSpec cards and by CardTypeRegistry.toCard for lifted ones; the shell checks it again before the fetch). The shell fetches it and inserts the returned HTML as-is, unsanitized, the same trust level as footer.text. The endpoint must therefore be a trusted first-party route, must never be derived from request data, and must escape any data it embeds in the fragment.

A card that cannot guarantee that can opt in with "sanitize": true (or sanitize=true on <@card>, or CardSpec.sanitize(true)). The shell then rebuilds the fetched fragment through the views attribute-allowlist sanitizer, the one behind the SANITIZED_HTML detail format, so script, on* handlers, unsafe URLs and unlisted attributes are dropped. The page must load the views toolkit; without it the card fails closed with E-JS-8 and paints nothing. The flag only affects src cards, and the default is unchanged (unsanitized).

Example:

CardSource s = CardSource.create("html", "welcome") .title("Welcome") .body("<p>Hello!</p>") .templateSink(page::captureTemplate) .build(); JsonMap frag = new HtmlCardType().toFragment(s); // {"template":"welcome"}
